correctness.rationale: The greedy arch decomposition is bijective on Dyck paths with the forced closing suffix. It gives \(n-k\) equal to total upward arch increments. A unique formal arch-height recurrence is solved by a geometric-height ansatz and quadratic, yielding \(C(z(1-z)/(1-x))\). Substitution and binomial extraction prove all coefficients. The dominant root \(\rho(u)\) is simple and uniquely smallest near \(u=1\), and square-root transfer/quasi-powers yields slope \(2/3\), variance slope \(4/27\), and a CLT. The standalone script directly checked 290512 Dyck words and independent bounded-defect transfer cells; finite tests are supplementary, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Arch factorization is established; the located prior fixed-defect Dyck work evaluates each defect through rational finite matrices and explicitly handles small defects, but does not give a single closed algebraic evaluation across all defects or a Gaussian limit for a linearly growing index. The four inspected primary sources treat individual-word arches, unrestricted/regular-language universality, or Dyck factors of an automatic word. A new all-defect Catalan substitution and nondegenerate quasi-powers analysis are proved. Unindexed equivalent lattice-path enumerators remain a genuine risk.

value.rationale: The global Catalan composition gives a complete uniform exact law for a natural subsequence-complexity invariant on all Dyck words, instead of a defect-by-defect matrix. It extracts exact coefficients for arbitrary semilength/index and establishes the previously absent typical-index Gaussian regime, with explicit nontrivial constants \(2/3\) and \(4/27\). This supplies a structural and probabilistic classification, not a routine small-table increment.
